title: Capture First, Decode Later
hook: When load is high, do not force insight. Capture the packet. Decode when capacity returns.
excerpt: A three-step protocol for keeping cognitive throughput without pretending every day is a deep-work day.
lede: High-output days and wipeout days are both real. The mistake is using the same workflow for both.
author: Nitish Chauhan

sections.heading: 1. Capture under load
sections.body: Dump the raw packet with almost zero formatting. Voice note, chat export, or a single markdown dump is enough.

sections.heading: 2. Park, do not polish
sections.body: Polishing under load burns the capacity you need to recover. Parking is the skill.

sections.heading: 3. Decode on a high day
sections.body: When fluency returns, compile: extract levers, decisions, and next actions. That is when agents earn their keep.

steps.label: Scan
steps.body: Skim for decisions and open loops.

steps.label: Cluster
steps.body: Group related packets into one arc.

steps.label: Compile
steps.body: Ship a note, lab, or task list.

takeaway: Treat mood-state as system state. Capture protocols must survive wipeouts, or the loop leaks.
caveat: Protocol sketch for personal systems design, not clinical advice.
